sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Passive Holding of Subsidiary Shares and Corporate Dividends

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Common Law (Alberta adopts common law; Canada operates a hybrid federal–provincial constitutional system under the Constitution Act, 1867, with civil law limited to Quebec; Alberta statutes govern incorporation, while federal AML, sanctions, and tax legislation apply concurrently)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA, provisional application since 2017)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP, in force 2018)
Canada–United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (in force 2021)
Canada–China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2014)
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by the 2007 Protocol; active DTAA)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), as amended, and FINTRAC reporting obligations; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17; United Nations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. U-2; Freezing Assets of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 21; Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. 1 (5th Supp.); Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, Part 2.1 (register of individuals with significant control); Alberta Business Corporations Act, RSA 2000, c. B-9, as amended (Alberta individuals-with-significant-control register and corporate transparency duties, effective for corporations incorporated in Alberta); FATF Mutual Evaluation Report of Canada (adopted 2024)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (including Articles of Incorporation filed under the Alberta Business Corporations Act)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille Convention (in force for Canada since 11 January 2024); Alberta-issued document authenticated by the Alberta Queen's Printer (provincial authentication authority) and apostilled; for non-Hague destination states, Global Affairs Canada authentication followed by consular legalization at the foreign embassy in Ottawa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status (official corporate registry extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Alberta Queen's Printer; consular legalization route for non-Hague states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and Extract of the Individuals-with-Significant-Control Register (UBO register)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Directors or officers of the corporation, countersigned by an Alberta-licensed notary public or corporate registered agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille (Alberta Queen's Printer); consular legalization route for non-Hague destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Director, Officer, and UBO Identity Documents (notarized passport and proof-of-address copies)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of each UBO's country of residence; notarized by the local notary in the jurisdiction of issuance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and Apostille in the UBO's home jurisdiction; English or French certified translation required where original documents are not in an official language of Canada; consular legalization where the UBO's home jurisdiction is not a Hague Convention member

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based FINTRAC-compliant screening of all directors, officers, and individuals holding 25% or more of shares or control, conducted before incorporation and before bank onboarding, against: (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List (implemented under the United Nations Act); (ii) Canadian autonomous sanctions regulations made under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice Laws Implementation regulations; (iii) the OFAC SDN List applied as industry-standard advisory screening; (iv) domestic Canadian politically exposed persons (PEP) databases covering federal, provincial, and municipal public-office holders, heads of state, and senior officials of foreign states; (v) FATF high-risk and monitored jurisdiction indicators; and (vi) adverse media and negative-news checks. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory where any UBO is resident in, or source funds originate from, a high-risk third country, or where the SPV is used for cross-border intercompany dividend flows.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry — Company Registry Operations (Service Alberta); official portal: https://www.alberta.ca/corporate-registry; name searches are conducted through the NUANS (Newly Upgraded Automated Name Search) system, accessible via licensed registry agents and Alberta Corporate Registry approved service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An Alberta corporation's name must contain a distinctive element and a legal element ('Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.', 'Ulc.', or the French equivalents), must be in English, French, or a juxtaposition of both, and must be expressed in Roman/Latin script. Non-Roman script names must be transliterated into Roman characters and verified through NUANS to confirm distinctiveness and absence of confusing similarity with existing Alberta, federal, extra-provincial, or NUANS-indexed foreign corporate names. A name that is merely descriptive, misdescriptive, or confusingly similar to an existing name is not registrable unless a consent or a 'resolved name' arrangement is accepted by the Director.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Insurance, Assurance, Loan and Investment Corporation, Credit Union, Cooperative, Retail Association (require enabling statute or financial regulator authorization)
College, University, Institute, Academy, School (where the name implies an educational or professional institution)

Engineer, Professional Engineer, Architect, Lawyer, Barrister, Solicitor, Notary, Physician, Surgeon, Pharmacist, Veterinarian, Accountant (require the consent of the relevant professional regulatory body)
Royal, Crown, Her Majesty, Government, Canada, Alberta, Municipality (reserved terms implying Crown or government patronage)
United Nations, Red Cross, Red Crescent, and other protected heraldic or international organization symbols
Names that are scandalous, obscene, contrary to public order, or that could reasonably be confused with an existing trade-mark or trade name in Canada
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the Alberta Corporate Registry issues a written refusal identifying the grounds (e.g., confusing similarity, prohibited token, or non-distinctiveness). The applicant may: (i) submit a revised name using the existing NUANS window or a new NUANS report; (ii) file a written request for reconsideration with the Director of the Corporate Registry, typically processed within 10–15 business days, attaching supporting evidence such as the consent of the senior-name holder or proof that the conflicting name is not in active use; (iii) obtain a consent letter from the prior user where confusion arises from a registered trade-mark or existing corporation; and (iv) as a final administrative-law remedy, apply to the Court of King's Bench of Alberta for judicial review or an order compelling registration. Each new name filing or NUANS submission attracts a fresh statutory fee, and the incorporation filing will not be accepted until a clear name is obtained.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible only to the extent that a licensed registered agent in Alberta provides a physical street address within Alberta (typically Calgary or Edmonton), maintains a registered office that can accept service of process, and holds corporate records at that address. A post-office box, mail-forwarding-only address, or an address located outside Alberta does not satisfy the Alberta Business Corporations Act registered-office requirement. For a passive equity holding SPV engaged in ISIC 6420/NAICS 551112, a virtual office through a commercial registered agent is generally accepted by Alberta authorities and Canadian banks, provided the agent's physical premises and document-custody functions are genuine.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: quantified probability of an unannounced physical inspection is approximately 8–12% in the first operating year for an unregulated passive HoldCo SPV with no financial-services license. The probability increases to 30–40% where a Canadian bank's enhanced due diligence or FINTRAC-reporting triggers require physical verification, or where the Alberta Corporate Registry, CRA, or a foreign competent authority identifies inconsistencies between the registered office, the individuals-with-significant-control register, and the SPV's stated passive investment purpose.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: NUANS Name Search Report and preliminary name clearance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta), submitted through a licensed registry agent
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory/registry-agent tariff: CAD 45 NUANS processing fee plus agent handling fee (prevailing market benchmark)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Articles of Incorporation filing fee (standard online filing under the Alberta Business Corporations Act)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory incorporation filing tariff: CAD 250 for online filing, per Alberta Corporate Registry fee schedule

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certificate of Status (official corporate registry extract for banking and counsel KYC bundle)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory certificate fee: online issuance CAD 50; certified hard-copy issuance higher

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered Office and Registered Agent services, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Private licensed corporate registered agent (commercial service provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: CAD 275–350 per year for an Alberta physical street address, service-of-process acceptance, and mail scanning

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate minute book and Individuals-with-Significant-Control (ISC) register setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate services provider (licensed registered agent or law firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: CAD 150–300 for physical/digital records custody, organizational resolutions, and ISC register preparation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, authentication, and Apostille of the corporate KYC bundle (Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Status, Certificate of Incumbency, UBO passport copies)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Local Alberta notary public; Alberta Queen's Printer (provincial authentication authority); Global Affairs Canada (federal authentication)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory authentication fee of CAD 25–50 per document plus notary fee of CAD 75–150 per signing session; additional courier and consular-legalization charges where the receiving state is not a Hague Apostille Convention member

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation legal due diligence and SPV structuring opinion (passive HoldCo, tax classification review, banking KYC alignment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Canadian law firm (Alberta-licensed corporate/income-tax counsel)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for an Alberta HoldCo SPV of moderate complexity: blended hourly rate CAD 400–600/hour or fixed engagement fee; jurisdiction-specific and fact-sensitive

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP, OFAC, UN Consolidated List, domestic sanctions, and adverse-media screening engine (initial entity and UBO screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Third-party compliance and KYC data provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market subscription or per-search benchmark for medium-risk corporate entity screening, including ongoing monitoring for the first year

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 9-13 (incorporation), s. 99 (registered office), s. 106 (officers), s. 114 (financial statements) and Alberta Regulations 2023-04/2024 (Corporate Registry online modernization)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registries Alberta), accessible through authorized Registry Agents or the Corporate Registry Online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1) filed under s. 9 ABCA; Certificate of Incorporation issued under s. 10(1) ABCA
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital requirement; shares may be issued at par or without par value for consideration fixed by the directors under ss. 24-25 ABCA; no escrow, capital deposit, or trust account rule applies to a standard private holding corporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: BE IT RESOLVED THAT: 1. The corporation accepts the subscription of 100 common shares from the sole incorporator at a consideration of CAD 1.00 per share, issued fully paid and non-assessable. 2. The registered office shall be at [address] in the City of [City], Alberta, as the statutory registered office pursuant to section 99 of the ABCA. 3. [Name] is appointed Chief Executive Officer, [Name] is appointed Corporate Secretary, and [Name] is appointed Chief Financial Officer, each to serve until the next annual general meeting. 4. The officers are authorized to execute all filings with the Alberta Corporate Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry Online (COR), Service Alberta; alternatively an Alberta-authorized Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name search request through COR or a registry agent to obtain a NUANS report; verify the proposed name is distinctive and does not include restricted words; reserve the approved name for 90 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and governing jurisdiction election
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search is refused or queried, file an alternative NUANS report and reservation request; any objection is cured by selecting a new distinctive name and paying the applicable search fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Articles of Incorporation form setting out share structure, director list, registered office notice, and permitted restrictions, if any; ensure all directors consent to act; pay the government filing fee online and obtain the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: NUANS report matching the approved name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried by COR, amend the deficient schedules or governing provisions and resubmit within the notice period; a formal rejection is cured by filing corrected Articles and paying the re-submission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Registered Office and Registered Records Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (for public filing) and the designated registered records office (law firm or corporate-services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Adopt the registered office location in Alberta, ensure it is a physical address, and designate a registered records office where statutory books, share registers, and minute books are maintained; produce and file the Notice of Registered Office with the Corporate Registry if required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registered office filing is rejected, confirm the address is a physical serviceable address in Alberta, correct the notice, and refile; any later change is remedied by filing a Notice of Change of Registered Office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Organizational Meeting and Written Resolutions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation (corporate internal action; no governmental filing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass unanimous written resolutions: issue the subscribed common shares, appoint the President, Secretary, and CFO, approve the bank mandate for the operating account, adopt the share certificate form, and fix the fiscal year end; complete these actions before any asset transfer or subsidiary acquisition.
required_dossiers: First board meeting minutes or unanimous written resolutions
Share certificate stubs and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a resolution is challenged, ratify it by a subsequent director resolution or shareholder resolution under s. 21 ABCA; disclose any director conflict under s. 120 ABCA and ensure interested directors abstain from voting.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings and Record Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Corporate Initial Return within two months of incorporation, disclosing registered office, director names, and principal business activity; maintain the corporate minute book and share ledger at the registered records office; open the corporate bank account with the board-approved signatory package.
required_dossiers: Minute book and corporate seal (if adopted)
Bank account opening resolution and signatory specimens
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Initial Return is late or deficient, file immediately with the CORPOR application, pay the administrative late fee, and update any director changes; a struck-off corporation may be revived under the ABCA curative reinstatement procedures.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - passive equity holding SPV with ISIC 6420 / NAICS 551112 scope; no industrial activity, manufacturing plant, or operational facility requiring a provincial industrial licensing board authorization
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - no provincially regulated operating permit is required for passive shareholding, dividend receipt, and subsidiary management; if a physical administrative office is opened, a municipal business licence from the relevant Alberta city (e.g., Calgary or Edmonton) may apply

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Alberta Environment and Protected Areas (AEPA) / Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) for federal coordination only
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no screening threshold or full EIA report trigger under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12 and the federal Impact Assessment Act, SC 2019, c 28, s 1, because the SPV conducts no physical development or designated industrial activity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - zero process wastewater, zero VOC, zero industrial waste handling; any office sanitization and domestic water discharges are de minimis and must comply with municipal sewer bylaws; no Alberta AEP discharge permit is triggered for pure administrative occupancy

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable for the passive holding activity itself; if physical office premises are established, the premises must obtain a fire safety certification under the Alberta Fire Code and a building occupancy inspection under the Safety Codes Act, RSA 2000, c S-1; if employees are later engaged, an occupational health and safety clearance under the Alberta OHS Act will apply.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada via CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online (BRO); Alberta corporate income tax is collected and administered by CRA under the Alberta Corporate Tax Act, with Alberta Treasury Board and Finance as the policy authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: After incorporation under the Canada Business Corporations Act or the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), register the corporation with CRA using Business Registration Online (BRO). CRA issues a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with program accounts, including the RC corporate income tax account and the RT GST/HST account. Non-resident corporations without a Canadian incorporation file Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) and provide director information, registered office/agent details, and evidence of corporate existence; CRA may require a Canadian representative for service. No separate Alberta TIN is issued; the CRA BN is the statutory tax identification number.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer; a corporation incorporated in Canada is deemed resident under ITA s. 250(4) and is taxable on worldwide income. A pure equity-holding SPV is not pass-through and cannot be disregarded for Canadian tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Canadian domestic law. Relevant statutory elections for a HoldCo include: Income Tax Act s. 85(1) tax-deferred rollover of property into a taxable Canadian corporation; s. 86 share-for-share exchange; s. 93(1) dividend election for distributions out of a foreign affiliate's exempt/ taxable surplus; s. 88(2) amalgamation; and Excise Tax Act s. 156 election between closely related corporations to treat intra-group supplies as made for nil consideration. No hybrid-mismatch election is available in Canada.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST — Federal Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax; Alberta applies only the 5% federal GST because the province has no provincial sales tax or provincial HST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — small supplier threshold of worldwide taxable supplies arising in a single calendar quarter or across four consecutive calendar quarters; for a non-resident corporation carrying on business in Canada, the threshold applies to taxable supplies made in Canada. Passive dividends and share dispositions are exempt financial supplies under Schedule V of the Excise Tax Act and do not count toward the registration threshold for a pure equity-holding SPV.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: CRA does not impose a mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-linked clearance gateway. E-invoicing is accepted if invoices satisfy the prescribed content requirements under the Excise Tax Act and are retained in English or French for six years. Large registrants are subject to mandatory electronic GST/HST filing through CRA-approved software; electronic records must be retained in an accessible machine-readable format.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exported from Canada by the supplier or on the supplier's behalf are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V of the Excise Tax Act if they are delivered to a destination outside Canada and supported by documentary proof of export. Services supplied to a non-resident may be zero-rated under ETA s. 23 where the service is performed for a non-resident and is not excluded (e.g., Canadian real property or goods). For a pure equity-holding SPV, dividends and share sales are exempt financial supplies, not zero-rated; input tax credits are recoverable only on inputs attributable to taxable supplies.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration / Canada Customs Coding Form B13A or electronic export reporting through the Canada Border Services Agency
Bill of Lading (ocean, air, rail, or truck) or equivalent transportation document
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank transfer documentation evidencing receipt of export proceeds
Written proof of export or delivery memorandum, including destination and date of export
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may audit export substantiation and deny zero-rating where documentary evidence does not establish export or delivery outside Canada. A zero-rating denial triggers reassessment, repayment of net GST/HST, recapture of claimed input tax credits, prescribed interest, and penalty provisions under the Excise Tax Act for false statements or omissions, including gross negligence penalties that can be up to 25% of the tax amount. Fraudulent export schemes can also attract criminal penalties, fines, and imprisonment for tax evasion, and the normal four-year reassessment period is extended in cases of misrepresentation or wilful default.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) exercises monetary authority and supervision of payment, clearing and settlement systems; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) supervises federally regulated banks; FINTRAC administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Canada maintains no discretionary foreign-exchange control administration under the Currency Act or the Financial Administration Act, and no central-bank or government approval is required for capital-account or current-account transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: CAD is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts under a free-floating exchange-rate regime; no Canadian restriction exists on dividend remittances, shareholder-loan repayments, or cross-border acquisition consideration. Non-resident dividend payments are subject to Part XIII withholding tax — statutory 25%, generally reduced to 5% under applicable tax treaties where the recipient owns ≥10% of the voting shares (e.g., Canada-US treaty Article 10(3)) — with NR4 information returns and Treasury remittance to the Receiver General. The Investment Canada Act (ISED review) is the sole material foreign-investment gateway and is not an exchange-control measure.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada repealed its Foreign Exchange Control Act in 1951; there is no statutory timeline, compulsory surrender ratio, minimum conversion percentage, or repatriation quota for export receipts or treasury inflows. Relevant compliance obligations are limited to FINTRAC cross-border currency reports for physical import/export of CAD 10,000 or more, large international EFT reports (EFTR) triggered at the CAD 10,000 threshold, and CRA reporting of foreign-source property (T1134/T1135) where applicable to the HoldCo.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Moderate viability. Canada does not issue an EU-style e-money institution (EMI) licence; payment service providers are being brought into the Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) regime, supervised by the Bank of Canada, with mandatory registration phased through 2024-2026. Offshore EMIs (e.g., FCA- or ECB-authorised) can provide rapid multi-currency onboarding and low-cost FX conversion but are not authorised Canadian deposit-taking institutions, cannot access Lynx high-value settlement, and attract elevated FINTRAC/PCMLTFA scrutiny. An offshore EMI is acceptable only as a secondary disbursement rail for small operational payments; it must never hold the SPV's primary treasury balance or capital-escrow funds.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No federal statute mandates physical attendance; the PCMLTFA 'reasonable measures' standard permits e-identification via secure video with government-issued photo ID, proof of address, and electronic KYC verification. In practice, Schedule I banks require an onboarding interview (physical or video) for all directors and material beneficial owners. Non-resident directors without a Canadian nexus are often asked to appear at a Canadian branch or to delegate signatory authority to a Canadian-resident officer or licensed corporate services provider under a board resolution. Remote account opening is permissible where the bank's global-transfer desk or a recognised financial intermediary performs identity verification; the strongest mitigation is early engagement with both the commercial banking team and the financial-crime compliance unit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Passive SPV with no employees, no local substance, and a balance sheet consisting solely of subsidiary shares
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and articles; Alberta corporate registry search result; registered-office certificate; group organisational chart; board resolution stating treasury and holding purpose; pro-forma financial statements; ISIC 6420 business plan; evidence of Canadian registered agent and, if appointed, Canadian-resident director.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) resident outside Canada controlling 25% or more of the HoldCo
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports; proof of residential address; source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements; audited financial statements of the ultimate parent; tax-residency certificates; executed UBO declaration; transactional trail from the originating regulated bank; written consent to OSFI/OFAC/UN/EU sanctions screening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intermediary chain located in a FATF-monitored or non-cooperative jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: FATF/CFATF classification memo; adverse-media and sanctions-screening results; stated economic rationale for the intermediary; source-of-funds evidence routed through licensed financial intermediaries; apostilled and notarised corporate and passport copies; pre-submission of the full file to the bank's financial-crime unit for preliminary transparency review.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume intercompany dividend and shareholder-loan flows portending alternative remittance or tax leakage
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer-pricing file aligned with OECD guidance and CRA Form T106; executed shareholder loan and equity subscription agreements; external Canadian tax opinion confirming Part XIII withholding position and treaty eligibility; treasury cash-flow model with a forecast dividend schedule; CRA NR4 and RC159 remittance procedure; commitment to quarterly reconciliation and audit rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs), including foreign PEPs, among directors or UBOs
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed PEP declarations; independent wealth-verification letter from a licensed advisor; source-of-funds substantiation (sale agreements, estate documents, dividends); enhanced monitoring protocol with a dedicated compliance contact; commitment to annual re-certification and audit-grade record retention.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan funding is routed by SWIFT MT103 from the overseas investor or group treasury to the HoldCo's Canadian Schedule I bank account. Recommended payment narrative: 'Capital Contribution — [Legal Entity Name] — [Board Resolution Ref]' with a bank-recognised purpose code (e.g., EQUI/CORP/CFIN or 'Capital Injection'). CAD-denominated transfers above ACSS thresholds settle through Lynx, Canada's high-value real-time gross settlement system (successor to LVTS). Pre-arrival steps include activating the receiving account, pre-validating the SWIFT BIC and account number, and issuing a spot FX instruction if the remittance currency is non-CAD. Both sending and receiving banks file FINTRAC EFTRs for transfers at or above CAD 10,000; the treasury archive must retain the covering board resolution, source-of-funds statement, MT103 confirmation, and bank credit advice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements of a pure equity-holding SPV comprise (i) downstream intercompany subordinated loans, (ii) operating expenditures, and (iii) upstream dividends. Dividend remittances are executed through SWIFT MT103 wires in CAD/USD/EUR; prior to release, the SPV must remit Part XIII withholding tax (statutory 25%, treaty-reduced as applicable) and file NR4 information returns. For acquisition consideration, the recommended rail is SWIFT MT103 with a board-approved settlement schedule and, where needed, a conditional escrow instruction. A documentary commercial letter of credit (UCP 600) is permissible only where the target transaction expressly requires a trade-finance instrument — atypical for an ISIC 6420 HoldCo. All outbound flows are sanctions-screened (OSFI/OFAC/UN/EU) and reconciled against the approved treasury cash-flow plan.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable spot and outright forward FX contracts (CAD/USD, CAD/EUR) executed under ISDA 2002 or a long-form confirmation with a Schedule I bank
FX swaps and cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge shareholder-loan and dividend-remittance exposures
Vanilla FX options (plain-vanilla calls and puts) traded under a negotiated ISDA/Credit Support Annex
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are legally permissible in Canada but not recommended for CAD because CAD is fully deliverable and NDF settlement introduces an avoidable USD-reference basis risk

Long-dated forward overlay for board-approved M&A pipeline commitments, limited to no-deal protection and termination clauses; all derivative activity requires a board resolution establishing prudent risk-appetite limits with no speculative trading mandate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return under section 263 of the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta (Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation or amalgamation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 100; continued non-compliance after Registrar's notice can trigger administrative dissolution or strike-off of the corporation from the Alberta Corporate Registry

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (including T106, T1134-B, and other ownership information schedules where applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after the end of the taxation year; balance of tax payable due within 2 months after year-end (3 months for qualifying Canadian-controlled private corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per month for up to 12 months; T1134 failure penalties up to CAD 24,000 per return; administrative loss of deduction rights under subsection 162(10) if filed more than 18 months late

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Audit is mandatory for distributing/public corporations and for any corporation where the shareholders have not unanimously consented to dispense with the appointment of an auditor (ABCA s. 161-162); pure equity holding SPVs may waive audit via unanimous shareholder consent; regulated or listed entities always require a licensed auditor
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/distributing enterprises; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) under the CPA Canada Handbook for eligible private SPVs

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate annual UBO filing is currently administered for Alberta-incorporated corporations; the Alberta Annual Return confirms current directors and officers, and share transfers must be recorded in the register of members upon each issuance or transfer; director changes must be notified to the Alberta Corporate Registry within 15 days; if the entity were incorporated federally under the CBCA, an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register is mandatory and ISC information is confirmed annually with Corporations Canada

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 120 - 350 per year (typical annual fee for Alberta registered office and registered agent services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 - 9,000 per engagement (typical certified audit fee for a small pure equity holding SPV)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined general rate (Federal Part I 15% + Alberta provincial 8%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No small business deduction applies to passive dividend and capital-gain income of an equity-holding SPV. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) earning aggregate investment income is subject to a federal refundable Part I top-up tax of 10 2/3% (33 2/3% combined incidence with Alberta's 8%), refundable through the Refundable Dividend Tax On Hand (RDTOH) account when taxable dividends are subsequently paid. Manufacturing and processing credits, the 9% small business rate and the general federal digital-services incentives are unavailable to a pure holding entity. If the SPV is not Canadian-controlled, the combined corporate rate remains a flat 23% with no refundable account mechanics. A non-resident-owned investment corporation (NROIC) election under Part XIV may partially displace Part I tax on Canadian-source investment income, but is narrowly restricted and requires an approved information return.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Canada Revenue Agency; filed through certified E-file software or the CRA 'My Business Account' portal; Alberta corporate income tax is collected by CRA on behalf of the Province of Alberta with the provincial schedules AB-1, AB-5 and AB-10 attached to the single consolidated T2 filing)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T2 return must be filed within 6 months after the end of the taxation year (fiscal period end), irrespective of the accounting year end; no discretionary extension of the filing deadline is granted by the CRA. Balance of corporate tax payable is due within 2 months for non-CCPCs and within 3 months for CCPCs after the year-end; Alberta's provincial portion follows the federal due dates. Late filing accrues prescribed daily compound interest plus the penalty described below.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business Number (9-digit BN plus RT/RC account code), legal registered name, Alberta jurisdiction identifier, fiscal period start and end dates, NAICS 551112 / ISIC 6420 code, corporation type and provincial code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident SPV must first create a programme account through Form RC1 and must file a T2 if it carries on a business in Canada, has a Canadian permanent establishment, disposes of taxable Canadian property, or derives Canadian-source passive income. The identification panel must clearly indicate 'non-resident' and attach Form T1134 foreign-affiliate reporting schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Summary – Line 50 (Net income before taxes)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income computed under IFRS/ASPE for the SPV including dividends received, interest income, capital gains, and any intercompany management fees or financing income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source passive income is re-determined under Schedule 1 and must be segregated from Canadian-source income; Part I tax applies to the entire taxable income of a Canadian-resident SPV regardless of the residency of the ultimate shareholder.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1 – Line 18 (Taxable dividends received from taxable Canadian corporations – s. 112 deduction)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 100% deduction for taxable dividends paid by a taxable Canadian corporation out of its safe income; eliminates double taxation at the holding level on Canadian subsidiary distributions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The s. 112 deduction applies to taxable Canadian corporations only; dividends from non-resident foreign affiliates must be processed under the s. 113/90 separate-entity mechanism and cannot be deducted at line 18 without a dangerous mismatch.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 1 – Line 40 (Taxable capital gains – 50% inclusion rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: One-half inclusion of net capital gains on dispositions of shares of underlying Canadian subsidiaries or foreign affiliates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A disposition by the SPV of shares in a Canadian subsidiary constitutes a disposition of taxable Canadian property under s. 115(1)(b); Part I tax applies and Part XIII withholding of 25% must be withheld on the purchase price unless an s. 116 certificate is obtained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income minus the s. 112 dividend deduction and other permitted loss carryforwards; the definitive base for federal Part I and Alberta provincial tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident companies cannot claim the s. 110 personal deductions; the line 56 computation must also be reconciled with Schedule 1 adjustments for transfer-pricing or GAAR recharacterizations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Summary – Line 63 (Part I tax payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Federal basic Part I tax at 15% on taxable income, reduced by the 10% federal abatement for income allocated to Alberta and by federal foreign-tax credits, but never below zero.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The federal abatement is allowed only where the corporation is resident in Alberta or has a permanent establishment in Alberta; treaty protection of the SPV's income does not displace the abatement computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 6 – Federal Foreign Tax Credit; T2 Alberta Schedule AB-5 – Alberta Foreign Tax Credit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign withholding taxes imposed on dividends and interest received from offshore subsidiaries, computed on a country-by-country basis and applied against both federal and Alberta tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit claims require contemporaneous proof of foreign tax paid (certificates of assessment or Form NR4 equivalents); post-payment treaty refunds must be reported and reconciled.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Schedule 7 – Aggregate Investment Income (CCPC only)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of refundable Part I tax and RDTOH for a Canadian-controlled private corporation with passive investment income; the RDTOH account is refunded at 38 1/3% when taxable dividends are paid to shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a CCPC is controlled by a non-resident person or by a public corporation it ceases to be a CCPC; the equity structure in the composite key must be evidenced to avoid an erroneous claim of small-business treatment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Not claimable on passive equity and dividend income; the schedule should be left at zero where line 50 income is exclusively dividends, interest and capital gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A pure equity-holding SPV cannot allocate an active business limit; erroneous claims are subject to s. 163(2) gross-negligence penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T2 Alberta Schedule AB-1 – Alberta Corporate Tax Computation at 8%
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Alberta provincial tax computed on taxable income allocated to an Alberta permanent establishment at the flat 8% rate; no Alberta capital tax or payroll tax on dividend-only companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An SPV with its registered office and directors' meeting location in Alberta will typically have a permanent establishment in Alberta; provincial schedules are mandatory even for opaque intermediate holding structures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Form T106 – Transfer Pricing Disclosure; Form T1134 – Foreign Affiliate Information Return
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory annual disclosure of every non-arm's length transaction (including management fees, interest, guarantees, dividends and share subscriptions) between the SPV and related Canadian / foreign entities; T1134 reports debt, surplus, and the 5%–10% ownership of each foreign affiliate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: T1134 late-filing carries a $2,500 per-affiliate per-month penalty (maximum 24 months) and forfeits access to the safe-income-on-hand regime used to reduce future s. 113 dividend withdrawals; a foreign parent must ensure parallel CRA filings are complete before the T2 assessment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filed T2 returns incur a penalty of 5% of the balance of tax payable plus 1% per complete month of delay for up to 12 months; a repeat/continued default doubles the initial 5% to 10%. Daily compound statutory interest at the CRA prescribed rate is added to the unpaid balance from the filing-due date. Failure to file the T1134 triggers the per-affiliate monthly penalty plus loss of foreign affiliate elections. CRA registration under s. 227.1 of a certificate against the SPV's assets follows without judicial intervention.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% Part XIII withholding tax applies to dividends paid by a Canadian-resident corporation to a non-resident shareholder, including a foreign parent SPV, unless a treaty reduction is successfully invoked.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a reduced treaty rate, the non-resident payee must complete Form NR301 (residents of the United States) or Form NR302 (residents of other treaty jurisdictions) and file with CRA before the dividend distribution, attaching a valid Certificate of Residence issued by the foreign tax authority (e.g., IRS Form 6166 for the US). CRA issues an approved copy to the payor who then withholds at the treaty rate. Treaty-based reduction is not automatic; where approval is pending, the payer must withhold 25% and the payee files Form NR7-R claiming a refund of over-withholding, supported by formal documentation, within the statutory period. Under Canada-US Article XXIX-A (Limitation on Benefits), a purely passive equity-holding SPV cannot secure a reduced 5% rate unless it satisfies the ownership, base-erosion and derivative-benefits tests; LOB failure restores the statutory 25% and exposes the payor to liability for un-withheld amounts.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: statutory Part XIII 25% (s. 212(1)(b)) is waived for arm's-length interest payments to unrelated non-residents under s. 212(1)(b)(vii); non-arm's-length and participating-debt interest remains fully subject to 25%, with treaty relief typically reducing this to 10-15% or 0% where the Canada-US protocol applies. Royalties: statutory Part XIII of 25% applies to patent, trademark and know-how payments; Canada-US treaty Article XII reduces royalty withholding to 10% for patents and industrial information and 0% for certain software and copyright payments to a US resident beneficial owner. All Part XIII amounts must be remitted to CRA by the 15th day of the month following payment, with Form NR4-B annual statements filed for every non-resident payee; a failure to withhold makes the SPV absolutely liable for the gross amount and defeats the subsequent refund.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canada imposes no monetary de minimis threshold for transfer-pricing documentation. Contemporaneous records documenting arm's-length terms of every non-arm's length cross-border transaction are conditionally required to defeat the s. 247(3) penalty of 10% of any net adjustment exceeding the lesser of 10% of gross revenue and C$3,000,000 in a given year. Country-by-Country Reporting (CbCR) is mandatory only for MNE groups with annual consolidated revenue of €750 million (approximately C$1.1 billion); otherwise the SPV must still maintain full Master File/Local File-equivalent documentation to satisfy CRA's IC 87-2 'reasonable efforts' requirement.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada does not operate a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime; substance is instead enforced through the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (s. 245), the foreign-affiliate 'active business' test under s. 95(1), and treaty Limitation-on-Benefits provisions. A zero-employee, zero-premise SPV interposed solely to extract dividends, generate deductible interest, or procure treaty rates will be recharacterized by CRA as a conduit: GAAR may eliminate the entire benefit and impose a 25% penalty; CRA will deny DTA relief under Article XXIX-A for failure of the ownership/base-erosion test; the SPV's income becomes fully taxable Part I at 23% and future dividends are trapped by Part XIII without credit. The Alberta 'economic substance' proxy is fixed by several factors, including the location of board meetings, presence of a treasury function, and evidence of commercial decisions; an SPV with no employees, no premises and no independent business purpose is the single strongest red flag for a CRA transfer-pricing audit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and False T2 Declarations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of dividend or interest income from the T2, deliberate understatement of taxable capital gains on a subsidiary sale, false declarations committed by the SPV directors, knowingly failing to file Form T1134 for foreign affiliates, or concealment of a disposition of taxable Canadian property from CRA.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income Tax Act s. 239(1): fine between 50% and 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment for up to 2 years per count; Criminal Code s. 380(1) fraud over C$5,000 attracts imprisonment up to 14 years. Civil gross-negligence penalty of 50% of the misstated amount under s. 163(2), plus prescribed compound interest. Voluntary disclosure does not protect willful or impossible-to-correct evasion, and the CRA audit may extend to the look-back period of 4-10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally liable for the SPV's unpaid Part I and Part XIII amounts under s. 227.1; CRA may register certificates and freeze directors' personal assets through exigible notification. Directors who signed the false T2 face personal criminal prosecution for evasion, travel restrictions at Canadian border crossings, loss of director eligibility under the Alberta Business Corporations Act, and civil actions by minority shareholders under the oppression remedy (ABC A s. 242).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a paper-only Alberta corporation with no employees, no premises, and no commercial decision-making that is interposed into a Canadian operating group to strip dividends with the principal purpose of avoiding Part XIII withholding, multiplying treaty benefits, or generating artificial deductions through intercompany loans.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: GAAR (s. 245(3)) retroactively recharacterizes the transaction, disallowing all tax benefits; 25% additional penalty of the disallowed benefit is imposed under s. 245(4); a failure on LOB/PPT treaty tests restores full 25% Part XIII withholding. CRA's offshore investment bulletin conducts a separate anti-conduit investigation, and the SPV may be subject to substantive penalties for unsupported management-fee invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who orchestrated the conduit will be treated as jointly liable for all re-assessed corporate tax, penalties, and interest; the Alberta courts may pierce the corporate veil to the directors' personal assets where the SPV is a façade, and the Crown may use the 'directing mind' doctrine to ground criminal liability on the shareholders rather than only the entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unremitted Part XIII Withholding and Information Returns
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to withhold 25% on dividends paid to a foreign parent SPV, payment of interest to a non-arm's-length non-resident lender without withholding, failure to remit with the 15th-of-the-month deadline, or failure to prepare NR4-B returns and obtain NR301/NR302 CRA approval before treaty withholding.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The unwithheld amount is an absolute liability and a debt to the Crown under s. 227(9); CRA assesses the SPV for the gross amount, adds daily compound prescribed interest from the due date, and imposes a 10% civil penalty for failure to withhold in addition to the interest; the failure to file NR4 information returns adds a C$1,000 summary conviction fine per return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under s. 227.1, directors are jointly and severally liable with the corporation for every unremitted Part XIII amount if the SPV defaults and the director knew or ought to have known of the failure; the due-diligence defense requires proof of an active and functioning supervision system, not nominal delegation; directors who resign after the arrears accrued remain liable; CRA can seek a departure embargo and asset-preservation order preventing the director from leaving Canada until the withholding debt is settled.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of contemporaneous comparability evidence for intercompany interest rates, management fees, guarantee premiums, and equity subscriptions; or deliberate manipulation of the SPV's transfer-pricing margins such that the annual net adjustment exceeds the lesser of 10% of gross revenue and C$3,000,000; failure to file Form T106 within the prescribed time.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer-pricing penalty equal to 10% of the net adjustment for the year (under s. 247(3)) where reasonable arm's-length efforts are absent; CRA may make secondary adjustments that deem excess capital to be a shareholder loan, causing a 25% Part XIII withholding tax; loss carrybacks cannot be used to extinguish the adjusted income; Form T106 late filing is a separate penalty of C$100 to C$7,500 per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be assessed personally for the TP penalty under the general directors' liability provision where the penalty constitutes a debt of the corporation and the SPV is insolvent; in Alberta insolvency courts will also entertain wrongful-trading claims against officers who authorized intercompany pricing without a proper functional analysis, potentially voiding director indemnity insurance.
